title: pricing-packaging-scratchpad
content:
Quick scratchpad for pricing / packaging ideas — very rough. Notes to self and quick unit-econ checks for hosted API + simple tiering.

Context / goal:
- Want simple PLG-friendly tiers that map to usage patterns: hobby/dev -> startup -> growth -> enterprise.
- Keep hosted pricing competitive vs other hosted APIs but preserve margin.
- Encourage committed (Dedicated) customers to move off hosted with clear pricing incentives.
- Provide predictable meter for evals / embeddings / chat.

Assumptions (baseline numbers for calc) — update with real infra telemetry later:
- Average token served cost (including GPU amortization, infra, bandwidth, caching hit adjustments, overhead): estimate between $0.0005 and $0.002 per 1k tokens depending on model and caching. Use conservative default $0.001 / 1k tokens for mid-sized model (e.g., 13B quantized).
- Embeddings unit cost: assume cheaper per inference but smaller input size; treat 1 embedding call ≈ 500 tokens for bucket pricing (for econ comparison) or price per embedding separately.
- Median session length (chat) = 800 tokens request+response per session (for product customers).
- Cold KV-cache miss rate: 20% for typical workloads, reduces effective cost.
- Support & infra overhead allocation: add +20% to raw inference cost for platform, monitoring, storage, billing etc. So blended cost = baseline * 1.2.

Quick unit-econ table (rounded):
- Raw model inference cost: $0.001 / 1k tokens
- Blended cost (1.2x): $0.0012 / 1k tokens
- Margin target (hosted) target gross margin 60% -> price must be >= blended / (1 - margin) = 0.0012 / 0.4 = $0.003 / 1k tokens -> price floor ~$0.003/k tokens

Rough pricing candidates (hosted API, per-1k tokens):
- Developer / hobby: $0.004 / 1k tokens (good for small experiments, slightly above floor)
- Startup: $0.0035 / 1k tokens (volume discount via plan commit)
- Growth / product: $0.0025 / 1k tokens (for larger committed customers — we keep margin via volume & caching improvements)
- Enterprise / Reserved: negotiate — baseline $0.002 / 1k tokens with committed monthly spend and SLA.

BUT note: real customers sensitive to pct discounts vs absolute cost; competitors advertise $0.001-$0.002/k for small models — need to differentiate via reliability, rollouts, privacy, and predictable billing.

Monthly example consumption -> bill -> margin (approx):
- Small app: 5M tokens/month = 5,000 * price_per_1k
  - at $0.004/k => $20/month revenue; blended cost = 5,000 * 0.0012 = $6 -> gross margin $14 (70%)
- Mid app: 200M tokens/month -> at $0.003/k => $600 revenue; cost = 200,000 * 0.0012 = $240 -> margin $360 (60%)
- Large app (pre-enterprise): 2B tokens/month -> at $0.0025/k => $5,000 revenue; cost = 2,000,000 * 0.0012 = $2,400 -> margin $2,600 (52%)

Embedding pricing idea (separate meter):
- Price per embedding call (vector produced) = $0.0004 per embedding (assuming avg 512 tokens input), or convert to per-1k-token equivalent ~ $0.0008/k tokens.
- Offer bundle discounts: e.g., 100k embeddings/month for $25 (effective $0.00025 per embed) for early-stage teams.

Free tier / credits:
- Free: 50k tokens + 10k embedding credits (for trial). Enough for a few API experiments.
- Free rate-limit low to prevent abuse.

Metering & billing UX thoughts:
- Show token breakdown in console: prompt vs completion vs cached hits (saves) — helps users optimize.
- Provide token estimate APIs in SDK.
- Offer cost-sim calculator (console + CLI) with real model profiles.

Tier design (straightforward):
- Free: 50k tokens + 10k embeddings, basic rate limit, community support.
- Developer: $10 / month -> includes 2M tokens + 5k embeddings, overage $0.005/k (high to push upgrades) or automatic switch to pay-as-you-go pricing.
- Startup: $99 / month -> includes 50M tokens + 50k embeddings or equivalent credit, discounted pay-as-you-go at $0.0035/k; onboarding docs + 2 seats.
- Growth: $499 / month -> includes 500M tokens + 500k embeddings, discounted at $0.0025/k; team seats + basic SSO
- Enterprise / Dedicated: custom pricing (monthly commit + lower per-token + SLA). Encourage committed discounts if commit >= X tokens/month or $Y/month.

Notes on Dedicated (reserved capacity) pricing model:
- Two components: base capacity fee (per-GPU or per-inference-unit) + per-token usage for burst/overage.
- Example: dedicated pool price $Z / vGPU-month + included baseline throughput measured in tokens/hr. Overages priced lower than hosted per-token.
- Need clear migration path: e.g., if commit >= $20k/month -> 30% discount vs hosted PS price.

Potential pitfalls / TODOs:
- Need to plug in actual infra telemetry: avg tokens/sec per GPU, infra cost per GPU-month (spot vs reserved), median cache hit rate per workload. -> Linked ticket JIRA-PRIC-214.
- Confirm embedding cost with infra team (Rohit).
- Evaluate price sensitivity via experiments (discount vs sign-up conversion). A/B test promo credits.
- Legal: validate enterprise contract language for data residency when offering lower per-token price (customers will ask).

Open questions / discussion points:
- Should we price chat differently from generation? (chat tends to re-send history -> higher tokens). Maybe charge per-turn or per-message band? Simpler to keep token-based but provide tooling to truncate history.
- How to handle function/tool calling (structured outputs) — higher latency cost for model calls + external tool orchestration. Tag as separate meter or bundled into token bill?
- For quality-based pricing (larger models cost more): how many SKU tiers (1-3) do we expose vs many models? Simpler for customers to pick "fast/cheap" vs "best-quality".

Immediate next steps for this doc (me):
- Pull infra cost sheet (infra team) and update blended cost per model family. (Rohit)
- Draft simple pricing page copy for website + console pricing calculator. (Samira to draft)
- Propose A/B experiments for free credit sizes and Developer tier price points. Track conversion.

References / links (placeholders):
- confluence/pricing/overview (note: draft pricing strategies)
- JIRA-PRIC-214 (unit-econ data collection)
- slack:#pricing (discussion thread link)

Random notes / brain-dumps:
- Might be useful to expose a "cost-estimate" header on streaming responses so clients can show an estimate before rendering (for UX).
- Consider per-call metadata tags so we can attribute expensive requests to features for better cost allocation.
- On embeddings: emphasize per-embed SLA + nightly batch embedding job credits for vector DB imports (different pricing bucket).

-- Ava

(End of scratchpad — keep rough. Will move into structured PRD once numbers validated.)
